cases.sentence: Граф, распустив карты веером, с трудом удерживался от привычки ___ и всему смеялся.
cases.explain: «послеобеденного сна» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The count, holding his cards fanwise, kept himself with difficulty from dropping into his usual after-dinner nap, and laughed at everything. The young people, at the countess’ instigation, gathered round the clavichord and harp. Julie by general request played first. After she had played a little air with variations on the harp, she joined the other young ladies in begging Natásha and Nikoláy, who were noted for their musical talent, to sing something. Natásha, who was treated as though she were grown up, was evidently very proud of this but at the same time felt shy.

cases.sentence: Жюли первая, по просьбе всех, сыграла на арфе пиеску с варияциями и вместе с ___ стала просить Наташу и Николая, известных своею музыкальностью, спеть что-нибудь.
cases.explain: «другими девицами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.

cases.sentence: Сундук в коридоре был место печалей женского ___ дома Ростовых.
cases.explain: «молодого поколения» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Running into Sónya’s room and not finding her there, Natásha ran to the nursery, but Sónya was not there either. Natásha concluded that she must be on the chest in the passage. The chest in the passage was the place of mourning for the younger female generation in the Rostóv household. And there in fact was Sónya lying face downward on Nurse’s dirty feather bed on the top of the chest, crumpling her gauzy pink dress under her, hiding her face with her slender fingers, and sobbing so convulsively that her bare little shoulders shook. Natásha’s face, which had been so radiantly happy all that saint’s day, suddenly changed: her eyes became fixed, and then a shiver passed down her broad neck and the corners of her mouth drooped.

cases.sentence: Действительно, Соня в своем воздушном ___, приминая его, лежала ничком на грязной полосатой няниной перине, на сундуке и, закрыв лицо пальчиками, навзрыд плакала, подрагивая своими оголенными плечиками.
cases.explain: «розовом платьице» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.

cases.sentence: А Николай мне cousin... надобно... ___... и то нельзя.
cases.explain: «сам митрополит» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “It’s all very well for you … I am not envious … I love you and Borís also,” she went on, gaining a little strength; “he is nice … there are no difficulties in your way. … But Nikoláy is my cousin … one would have to … the Metropolitan himself … and even then it can’t be done. And besides, if she tells Mamma” (Sónya looked upon the countess as her mother and called her so) “that I am spoiling Nikoláy’s career and am heartless and ungrateful, while truly … God is my witness,” and she made the sign of the cross, “I love her so much, and all of you, only Véra … And what for? What have I done to her? I am so grateful to you that I would willingly sacrifice everything, only I have nothing. …”

cases.sentence: —сказала она вдруг, как будто догадавшись о ___ огорчения кузины, — верно, Вера с тобой говорила после обеда?
cases.explain: «настоящей причине» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Sónya,” she suddenly exclaimed, as if she had guessed the true reason of her friend’s sorrow, “I’m sure Véra has said something to you since dinner? Hasn’t she?”

cases.sentence: Ты видишь, как он с ней ___...
cases.explain: «целый день» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Yes, these verses Nikoláy wrote himself and I copied some others, and she found them on my table and said she’d show them to Mamma, and that I was ungrateful, and that Mamma would never allow him to marry me, but that he’ll marry Julie. You see how he’s been with her all day … Natásha, what have I done to deserve it? …”

cases.sentence: Вот дяденьки Шиншина брат женат же на ___, а мы ведь троюродные.
cases.explain: «двоюродной сестре» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Sónya, don’t believe her, darling! Don’t believe her! Do you remember how we and Nikólenka, all three of us, talked in the sitting room after supper? Why, we settled how everything was to be. I don’t quite remember how, but don’t you remember that it could all be arranged and how nice it all was? There’s Uncle Shinshín’s brother has married his first cousin. And we are only second cousins, you know. And Borís says it is quite possible. You know I have told him all about it. And he is so clever and so good!” said Natásha. “Don’t you cry, Sónya, dear love, darling Sónya!” and she kissed her and laughed. “Véra’s spiteful; never mind her! And all will come right and she won’t say anything to Mamma. Nikólenka will tell her himself, and he doesn’t care at all for Julie.”

cases.sentence: Соня приподнялась, и котеночек оживился, глазки заблистали, и он готов был, казалось, вот-вот взмахнуть хвостом, вспрыгнуть на ___ и опять заиграть с клубком, как ему и было прилично.
cases.explain: «мягкие лапки» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Natásha kissed her on the hair. Sónya sat up. The little kitten brightened, its eyes shone, and it seemed ready to lift its tail, jump down on its soft paws, and begin playing with the ball of worsted as a kitten should.
